title: Bounded halving routine
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $b$ a Boolean, and $s$ a machine state whose seven register values are at most $B$. The machine has a run on input $x$ from label $	ext{hv}(b,0)$ and state $s$ to label $	ext{od}(b)$ and state obtained from $s$ by setting $C=0$ and $T= igl loor{s.T/2^{s.C} igrfloor}$, with the run guard satisfied at every configuration before its endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: Every register in $s$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, $b$ a Boolean
value, and $s$ a machine state whose seven register values are all at most $B$. Starting
from state $s$ at the halving routine's initial phase, the machine reaches the state at
the bit-test phase with counter $C=0$ and scratch register $T=\lfloor
s.T/2^{s.C}\rfloor$, while satisfying the run's preconditions and register bound
throughout.
